correctness.rationale: On KG(n,2), strict convexity and total unimodularity of root-anchored edge difference constraints force integral norming potentials; diameter two implies range 0,1,2. Their extreme zero/two sets are disjoint cross-intersecting edge families in K_n. The two-nonsingleton family inequality a+b<=max(n,6), the singleton extremum E_n=N(2n-3)-(2n-5)^2, and the balanced binary B_n=floor(N^2/4) yield the maximum with a distinct n=6 equality exception, 7<=n<=10 three-level winners, n=11 tie and n>=12 balanced binary winners. Independently exact enumeration corroborated the n=6 size profiles (1,8),(2,4),(4,2),(8,1) and n=7 singleton profiles. Infinite statement uses the combinatorial inequality and arithmetic comparisons.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration n=6,7 only; all-order bounds require and receive independent analytic combinatorial reasoning.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The all-graph complement-C4-free theorem cannot be applied to KG(n,2): its missing-edge graph J(n,2) contains 4-cycles. Borg bounds different family sum/product under different assumptions; neither gives a centered-variance optimum under disjointness.
